Stage 3 · Grammar

Grammar

I always… · I don't… · Do you…?
FormUseExample
adverbbefore the verbI always drink coffee.
We usually go out.
He always drinks coffee.
She sometimes works late.
negativedon't / doesn't + verbI don't watch TV.
We don't eat meat.
She doesn't eat meat.
He doesn't smoke.
questionDo / Does + verbDo you drink coffee?
Do we start at nine?
Does he work here?
Does she cook?
How often?asking frequencyHow often do you exercise?
How often does she read?
  • Frequency adverb goes BEFORE the verb: I usually get up at 7. She never eats meat.
  • Negative: I/you/we/they → don't + verb. he/she/it → doesn't + verb (no -s!): He doesn't work.
  • Question: Do you…? / Does she…? Short: Yes, I do. / No, she doesn't.
  • How often…? → always / usually / often / sometimes / never / once a week.

→ Wh- questions (what, where, when, who, why) come next.

🔧 Build it yourself
  • 🔧 Build it yourself
  • Build it: I drink coffee → I ALWAYS drink coffee (adverb BEFORE the verb) → I DON'T drink tea.
  • ⚠ Не пью / ішпеймін = DON'T drink — English needs don't + verb, and only ONE 'no' in the sentence.

🔊 The Tuareg — Oxford Navigate audiolisten, then answer
1The tagelmust is a piece of cloth.
2Women wear the tagelmust.
3It is often blue.
4It is sometimes black.
5Men wear it in the house.
6The sun and wind are strong in the Sahara.
Why these answers

The tagelmust is a long cloth Tuareg MEN wear on the head and face — often blue, sometimes black. They wear it outside (not in the house) because the sun and wind are strong.
